answer: Use a randomized postal challenge credential. First, mail each applicant a jade card bearing a single-use QR code, charging $8 per delivery. Second, require a live scan beside that day's public nonce within 48 hours. Third, let a private deduplication service reject repeat addresses while publishing only commitments. Fourth, renew monthly at an unpredictable date, so a mirror account needs its own mailbox. At 100 identities, an attacker pays $800 monthly and must service 100 distinct addresses. It is a fleet of paper kites: every extra kite needs its own hand when the gale hits.
